mainTopic: The sources that every service of every קרבן must be for its own type and its owner (לשמה), and why a קרבן offered שלא לשמה is still כשר.
overview: The גמרא first finishes rejecting the attempt to learn שינוי בעלים from שינוי קודש. Two of the differences turn out to be weak, but two strong ones remain, so the comparison fails. רב אשי then brings a direct source, 'ונרצה לו לכפר עליו', and the גמרא shows that this does not clash with רבי שמעון's use of the word 'עליו'. Next the גמרא looks for a source that קבלה must also be for the owner. It finds one in the פסוק about the איל נזיר and defends that reading against challenges based on the rules of כלל ופרט. The rule is then widened step by step: from the איל נזיר to all שלמים, and from שלמים to every קרבן, through the היקש of 'זאת התורה'. Finally the גמרא asks why a קרבן offered שלא לשמה is still כשר. It answers from 'מוצא שפתיך': such a קרבן becomes a נדבה. The גמרא then begins to explain why both פסוקים are needed, and that explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Two of the differences are weak, but two still stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that even though two of the differences between שינוי קודש and שינוי בעלים are not solid, the other two are. So the attempt to learn one from the other is still refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though two of the differences are not exact, at least two of them are exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up: two of its differences are weak, but two strong ones are enough to block learning שינוי בעלים from שינוי קודש. This line also sets up the next steps, which explain which two are weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the comparison between שינוי קודש and שינוי בעלים was knocked down by several differences. Now the גמרא grades those differences. Only two of them really hold up, but that is enough. One real difference is all you need to stop the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (here: two of the differences)
Not exact; not really accurate
Exact; truly accurate
At least; in any case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that because two differences fail, the comparison comes back to life. Two real differences are still left, and that is enough to keep the comparison broken.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּתַרְתֵּי לָאו דַּוְקָא,
phrases.english: And even though two are not precise,
phrases.notes: He means two of the differences listed just before, which tried to separate שינוי קודש from שינוי בעלים.

phrases.english: at least two are precise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּתַרְתֵּי לָאו דַּוְקָא, תַּרְתֵּי מִיהָא דַּוְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the earlier list of differences, which comes before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The attempt to learn שינוי בעלים from שינוי קודש stays refuted, because two real differences remain.

steps.title: Why 'the flaw is in the offering itself' is not a real difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא knocks down the difference that שינוי קודש damages the offering itself while שינוי בעלים is only a thought. Both are really just a thought, and in both cases the thought disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a change of owner, that its disqualification is not in the offering itself? Because it is only a thought. But a change of offering type is also only a thought! Rather, since he had that thought, he disqualified it. Here too, since he had that thought, he disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first weak difference. It shows that calling שינוי קודש a flaw 'in the offering itself' (פסולו בגופו) does not really separate it from שינוי בעלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim was that שינוי קודש is a flaw in the animal, while שינוי בעלים is only a thought in the mind of the one doing the service. The גמרא answers that שינוי קודש is also only a thought, since nothing physical changes in the animal. So if a thought disqualifies there, a thought can disqualify here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing the service with intent for a different owner
Doing the service with intent for a different type of offering
Its flaw is in the offering itself
Just a thought
He had that intent about it

phrases.english: What is different about a change of owner
that its disqualification is not in the offering itself?
Because it is merely a thought;

phrases.aramaic: שִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ נָמֵי מַחְשָׁבָה בְּעָלְמָא הוּא!
phrases.english: but a change of offering type is also merely a thought!
Rather, since he had that intent, he disqualified it;
here too, since he had that intent, he disqualified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא שִׁינּוּי בְעָלִים דְּלָא הָוֵי פְּסוּלוֹ בְּגוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two weak differences mentioned in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the difference of פסולו בגופו, not the whole refutation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שינוי קודש is also only a thought, so this difference does not really separate the two cases.

steps.title: The 'after death' difference fails according to רב פנחס
steps.stepSummary: The second weak difference was about the owner's death. רב פנחס בריה דרב מרי holds that שינוי בעלים applies even after the owner dies, so that difference falls away. Still, two real differences remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב פנחס son of רב מרי, who says a change of owner applies even after death, at least two differences are left to refute the comparison!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second weak difference. According to רב פנחס בריה דרב מרי, the owner's death does not separate the cases. Even so, two differences are still left, so the comparison stays broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One difference was that שינוי קודש applies even after the owner has died, while שינוי בעלים supposedly does not. רב פנחס says שינוי בעלים also applies after death, so this difference disappears. The גמרא stresses that two strong differences still remain.

keyTerms.meaning: After death (after the owner has died)
To refute; to break the comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Two of the differences (פסולו בגופו and the owner's death) fail, but two others still hold. So שינוי בעלים cannot be learned from שינוי קודש.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Pinchas son of Rav Mari,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ שִׁינּוּי בְעָלִים לְאַחַר מִיתָה –
phrases.english: who says a change of owner applies even after death –
at least two remain with which to refute!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי, דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ שִׁינּוּי בְעָלִים לְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second weak difference and confirms that two real differences still stand.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the 'after death' difference, and only according to רב פנחס בריה דרב מרי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רב פנחס, שינוי בעלים also applies after the owner's death, so the cases do not differ on this point.

steps.title: רב אשי brings a פסוק as the source
steps.stepSummary: Since the comparison failed, רב אשי learns the rule straight from a פסוק: 'ונרצה לו לכפר עליו'. The atonement must be for the owner and not for his friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: The פסוק says, 'And it shall be accepted for him to atone for him,' and not for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: Since learning from שינוי קודש did not work, רב אשי gives a brand-new source. A פסוק teaches directly that the offering's atonement is for its owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the offering is accepted 'for him' (ונרצה לו), so the atoning act must be done for the owner himself. Doing it for someone else is therefore wrong. This makes the comparison to שינוי קודש unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it shall be accepted for him to atone for him'
His friend; another person
Rather (dropping the earlier approach)

steps.whatToRemember: The source that one may not do the service for someone other than the owner is the פסוק 'ונרצה לו לכפר עליו', meaning for him and not for his friend.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the rule of שינוי בעלים its own source in the תורה, so it no longer depends on a comparison that kept being knocked down.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said,
the verse states:
"And it shall be accepted for him to atone for him" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:4

phrases.english: and not for his friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed comparison with a direct source from a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We tried to learn שינוי בעלים from שינוי קודש, but real differences broke the comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes straight from 'ונרצה לו לכפר', meaning for the owner and not for another.

steps.title: Isn't this verse already being used for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. The פסוק he used is already needed for רבי שמעון's teaching about responsibility for a lost offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this פסוק really come to teach that? It is needed for a ברייתא: 'And it shall be accepted for him to atone for him.' רבי שמעון says: if the offering was 'upon him' (he took on a personal obligation), he must replace it if it is lost. If it was not 'upon him', he does not have to replace it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's source from step 4. It says the same פסוק is already used by רבי שמעון for a completely different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a פסוק that is needed for one law cannot also be the source for another law. רבי שמעון reads the word 'עליו' to mean 'an obligation that rests on him'. If he said 'I take upon myself an offering', he must replace it if it dies or is lost. If he only set aside a specific animal, he does not have to. So the פסוק looks like it is already 'taken'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Responsibility to replace an offering that died or was lost
Upon him, meaning an obligation he took on personally

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of vows. 'עלי' ('I take upon myself an offering') creates a personal obligation, so the person must replace a lost animal. Setting aside 'this animal' with no personal obligation means he does not have to replace it.

phrases.english: But does this [verse] come for this?!
phrases.notes: 'This' is the פסוק רב אשי just used in step 4.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught [in a ברייתא]:
"And it shall be accepted for him to atone for him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:4

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
That which is upon him, he is responsible for it,
phrases.notes: He means an offering he personally promised. If it dies or is lost, he has to bring another one.

phrases.english: and that which is not upon him,
he is not responsible for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source רב אשי gave in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's use of 'ונרצה לו לכפר עליו' as the source that the blood must be for the owner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already needed for רבי שמעון's law of אחריות, so it seems it cannot also teach רב אשי's rule

steps.title: Why a personal promise makes you responsible
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי explains רבי שמעון's reasoning. Once someone says 'upon me', the offering is like a load sitting on his shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבדימי said: What is the reason? Once he said 'upon me', it is as if he is carrying it on his shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of the challenge. The גמרא brings an explanation of רבי שמעון's ברייתא to show that the word 'עליו' really is being read for that law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'עלי' places the duty on the person himself, not on one particular animal. So losing the animal does not free him. He keeps 'carrying' the duty until he actually brings an offering. This shows how firmly the word 'עליו' is tied to רבי שמעון's law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Upon me', the wording of a personal vow to bring an offering
His shoulder

phrases.english: And Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
What is the reason?
Since he said, "upon me,"
it is as if he carries it on his shoulder.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the ברייתא quoted in the challenge
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who says 'עלי' is like someone carrying the offering on his shoulders, so he must replace it if it is lost

steps.title: רב אשי learns from a different part of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רב אשי learns from 'ונרצה לו', not from the word 'עליו' that רבי שמעון uses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי was speaking about the words 'and it shall be accepted for him to atone'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Each teaching comes from a different part of the same פסוק, so there is no clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's law of אחריות is built on the word 'עליו'. רב אשי's rule, that the atonement must be for the owner, comes from 'ונרצה לו', meaning 'accepted for him'. Since they use different words, the פסוק can teach both laws.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall be accepted for him
He was saying, meaning he was referring to

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק, two teachings. 'ונרצה לו' teaches that the atonement must be for the owner (רב אשי). 'עליו' teaches responsibility to replace a lost offering (רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi
was speaking from "And it shall be accepted for him to atone."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מִוְּנִרְצָה לוֹ לְכַפֵּר קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the פסוק: each law comes from a different word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole פסוק is needed for רבי שמעון's law of אחריות
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון uses 'עליו', and רב אשי uses 'ונרצה לו', so both laws stand

steps.title: What about collecting the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that sources were found for שחיטה and זריקה being for the owner, and asks where we learn the same for קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for slaughtering and sprinkling. From where do we know it for collecting the blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question and sets up the next discussion. It wants a source that collecting the blood must also be done for the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the סוגיא has shown that שחיטה and זריקה must be for the sake of the owner. Collecting the blood (קבלה) is another main service, but none of the sources so far covered it. The גמרא now looks for a source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
Slaughtering the offering
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Collecting the blood in a vessel
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found slaughter and sprinkling,
phrases.notes: He means we found sources that these must be done for the owner.

phrases.english: collection [of the blood], from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן זְבִיחָה וּזְרִיקָה קַבָּלָה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the source for זריקה, the גמרא opens a search for a source for קבלה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that קבלה must also be performed for the sake of the owner

steps.title: Why we cannot learn קבלה from שחיטה and זריקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers learning קבלה from שחיטה and זריקה, and rejects it because those two have a stricter feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let us learn קבלה from שחיטה and זריקה. That does not work. שחיטה and זריקה are special, because doing them outside the Temple carries a punishment. So you cannot learn קבלה from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an easy answer to the question from Step 8 (learn קבלה from שחיטה and זריקה), and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה and זריקה are stricter than קבלה: someone who does them outside the Temple is punished, but not someone who does קבלה outside. Because they are stricter, a rule about them might not carry over to the weaker service of קבלה. So the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggestion that is about to be rejected)
What about X? It is special, because... (the standard way of breaking a comparison)
Collecting the animal's blood in a sacred vessel
One is punished for doing it outside the Temple

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that someone holds. The גמרא raises a possible source only so it can show why it fails, before giving the real source.

phrases.english: And if you would say: let us learn it from slaughter and sprinkling –
what about slaughter and sprinkling?
They are special, since each is a service for which one is punished if it is done outside!
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means outside the Temple courtyard. קבלה done outside does not carry that punishment, so it is weaker.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא לֵילַף מִזְּבִיחָה וּזְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects a possible answer to the question in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning קבלה from שחיטה and זריקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שחיטה and זריקה are punished when done outside the Temple; קבלה is not. That stricter feature breaks the comparison.

steps.title: רב אשי learns it from the ram of a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי finds the source in the פסוק about the ram of a נזיר. Since that פסוק is not needed for changing the type of offering, it teaches about changing the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: we learn it from the ram of a נזיר. The פסוק says: 'And the ram he shall make a sacrifice of שלמים.' This means the making of it must be for the sake of שלמים. But we already learned from other פסוקים that changing the type of offering is a problem. So this פסוק is free to teach a rule about changing the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the real answer to Step 8's question: the source for קבלה is the פסוק about the ram of a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יעשה' (he shall make) covers all the services, including קבלה. Read simply, the פסוק talks about the type of offering, but that rule is already known from elsewhere. Using the rule of 'אם אינו ענין', the extra פסוק is applied to the owner instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram a נזיר brings as a שלמים when his נזירות ends
If it is not needed for its own topic, apply it to another topic
Changing the type of offering (doing it in the name of a different קרבן)
Changing the owner (doing it for someone else)

steps.whyThisMatters: The word 'יעשה' is general enough to cover every service, which is exactly why it can include קבלה. That is what the next step will challenge.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
it comes from the ram of a nazir;
as it is written: "And the ram he shall make a sacrifice of peace-offerings" –
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:17

phrases.english: meaning that its making should be for the sake of a peace-offering;
and if it is not needed for changing the type of offering –
since he learns that from there,
phrases.notes: 'From there' means the פסוקים brought earlier on the דף that already teach about changing the type of offering.

phrases.english: apply it to changing the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַתְיָא מֵאֵיל נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the comparison in Step 9 fails, רב אשי gives a פסוק-based source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that קבלה must be done for the owner (from Step 8).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of the ram of a נזיר. 'יעשה' covers all services, and since changing the type of offering is learned elsewhere, the פסוק teaches about changing the owner.

steps.title: A challenge: the rule may only cover שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אבא argues that 'יעשה' followed by 'זבח' is a כלל ופרט, which would limit the rule to שחיטה only, so קבלה would not be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אבא said to רבא: Say that 'he shall make' is a general term and 'sacrifice' is a specific term. When a general term is followed by a specific one, the general includes only what the specific says. So only slaughter is included, and nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's source. It argues that, by the rules for reading פסוקים, the פסוק only covers שחיטה, not קבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of כלל ופרט, a general word that is followed by a specific word is limited to that specific case. 'זבח' comes from the same root as 'זביחה' (slaughter), so the פסוק would only demand that the slaughter be for the owner. That would remove קבלה, which was the whole point.

keyTerms.meaning: A general term followed by a specific one; the general is limited to the specific
Stated a general term / stated a specific term
Anything else

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Abba said to Rava:
Say: "he shall make" is a general term,
"sacrifice" is a specific term;

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל וּפְרָט – אֵין בַּכְּלָל אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁבַּפְּרָט;
phrases.english: with a general term and then a specific one, the general includes only what is in the specific;
so slaughter, yes; anything else, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא לְרָבָא, אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רב אשי read the פסוק in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's use of 'יעשה' to include all services, including קבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'יעשה' (general) followed by 'זבח' (specific) forms a כלל ופרט, which limits the rule to שחיטה alone.

steps.title: An incomplete general term is not read as כלל ופרט
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the word order of the פסוק makes 'יעשה' an incomplete general term, and the rule of כלל ופרט does not apply to one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had said 'he shall make שלמים a sacrifice', you would be right. But it actually says 'he shall make a sacrifice of שלמים'. So the general term is incomplete. Any incomplete general term is not read using the rule of כלל ופרט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי. It shows that the word order of the פסוק stops the כלל ופרט rule from working here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זבח' sits in the middle, between 'יעשה' and 'שלמים', so the general phrase is broken up and not complete. A כלל ופרט needs a complete general term before the specific one. Since that is missing, 'יעשה' stays broad and still covers קבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: An incomplete general term
We do not interpret it (by that rule)
Now that it is (actually) written

steps.whatToRemember: קבלה must be done for the owner. We learn this from 'יעשה' in the פסוק of the ram of a נזיר. It is not limited to שחיטה, because an incomplete general term is not read as כלל ופרט.

phrases.english: If it had been written: "he shall make peace-offerings a sacrifice" –
it would be as you say;
now that it is written: "he shall make a sacrifice of peace-offerings" –
it is an incomplete general term,
and any incomplete general term –
we do not interpret it by the rule of a general term and a specific term.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתִיב ״יַעֲשֶׂה שְׁלָמִים זֶבַח״ כִּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כלל ופרט challenge of Step 11 and keeps רב אשי's source standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule: כלל ופרט applies only to a complete general term.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יעשה זבח' is a כלל ופרט, so only שחיטה must be for the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because 'זבח' interrupts, 'יעשה' is an incomplete general term. כלל ופרט does not apply, so 'יעשה' includes all services, including קבלה.

steps.title: רבינא says the verse ends with a second general term
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers רב אחא בר אבא differently. We do learn from an incomplete general term, and 'לה׳' at the end of the פסוק is a second general term.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Actually, we can learn from it, and the word 'to ה׳' makes a general statement again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second answer to the challenge from Step 11. He says the פסוק is really a 'general, detail, general' pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 answered that an incomplete general term does not trigger כלל ופרט. רבינא disagrees and says we can use it. But 'לה׳' adds another general term after 'זבח', so the rule becomes כלל ופרט וכלל, which widens the law again beyond שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (used to keep an assumption the previous answer gave up)
We derive, we may learn from it
It went back and made a general statement again
A general term, a detail, then a general term: includes things similar to the detail

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא does not deny that 'יעשה' and 'זבח' form a כלל ופרט. He adds that 'לה׳' turns it into a three-part pattern, which gives a different result.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, we do derive [from it],
phrases.notes: He means that even an incomplete general term like 'יעשה' can be used in a כלל ופרט.

phrases.english: and "to ה׳" goes back and makes a general statement again.
phrases.notes: The full פסוק is 'ואת האיל יעשה זבח שלמים לה׳' (במדבר 6:17). 'לה׳' comes after the detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to Step 11's challenge, offered instead of Step 12's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the פסוק structure: it is כלל ופרט וכלל, not only כלל ופרט.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעשה זבח is a כלל ופרט, so only שחיטה needs to be for the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לה׳' adds a final general term, so other services like the detail are included.

steps.title: The two general terms are not the same size
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי objects. 'יעשה' covers only the main actions, but 'לה׳' covers everything done for ה׳, even minor services. Unequal general terms should not combine into a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא from דיפתי said to רבינא: But the first general term is not like the last one! The first includes only the main actions and nothing more. The last includes anything 'for ה׳', even pouring out the leftover blood and burning the sacrificial parts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges רבינא's new reading. He argues that the two general terms in the פסוק do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal כלל ופרט וכלל has two general terms of the same scope. Here 'יעשה' is narrow (main actions only). 'לה׳' is very broad and even covers שפיכת שירים and הקטרת אימורין, which are not essential to the offering. So he says the pattern should not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The first general term / the last general term
Actions, the main services done with the offering
Pouring the leftover blood onto the base of the מזבח
Burning the fat parts of the offering on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא לָא דָּמֵי כְּלָלָא קַמָּא לִכְלָלָא בָּתְרָא;
phrases.english: But the first general term is not similar to the last general term;

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָלָא קַמָּא – מְרַבֵּה עֲשִׂיּוֹת וְתוּ לָא,
phrases.english: the first general term includes actions and nothing more,
phrases.notes: 'יעשה' means 'shall do', so it only covers the main actions of the offering.

phrases.english: the last general term includes anything "to ה׳"
and even pouring the leftover blood and burning the sacrificial parts!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא דָּמֵי כְּלָלָא קַמָּא לִכְלָלָא בָּתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבינא's כלל ופרט וכלל reading from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that 'יעשה... זבח... לה׳' forms a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two general terms differ in scope (narrow vs. very broad), so they cannot frame the detail as a standard כלל ופרט וכלל.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל uses the rule even here
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that דבי רבי ישמעאל applies כלל ופרט וכלל even when the two general terms are not equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the school of רבי ישמעאל does expound generalities and details in a case like this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב אחא מדיפתי. The school that uses these rules applies them even when the general terms do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed that the two general terms must be equal. רבינא cites דבי רבי ישמעאל, who use כללי ופרטי even with unequal general terms. So the pattern still works here.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study house of רבי ישמעאל
The rules of general terms and details
In a case like this

phrases.english: But the school of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: בִּכְלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי דָּרֵישׁ כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא:
phrases.english: does expound generalities and details in a case like this:

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בִּכְלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי דָּרֵישׁ כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the method of a school of interpretation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Unequal general terms cannot form a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: דבי רבי ישמעאל apply the rule even with unequal general terms.

steps.title: Every service like slaughtering must be for the owner
steps.stepSummary: רבינא completes his derivation. In a כלל ופרט וכלל we include only things like the detail. The detail is a service that must be for the owner, so every service must be for the owner, and that includes קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A general term, a detail, and a general term: you include only things similar to the detail. Just as the detail spelled out is a service that we require to be for its owner, so too every service must be for its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finishes his proof. He applies כלל ופרט וכלל to show that every עבודה, like שחיטה, must be done for the sake of the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule includes items that share the detail's features. The feature chosen is 'a service of the offering'. Since קבלה is also a service, it is included, which answers Step 8's question.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to the detail
Spelled out, stated clearly in the פסוק
A service of the offering
For their sake (here: for the sake of the owner)

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא's source for קבלה: 'יעשה' (general), 'זבח' (detail), 'לה׳' (general). So every עבודה like שחיטה must be for the owner.

phrases.english: A general term, a detail, and a general term —

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט;
phrases.english: you may include only what is similar to the detail;
just as the detail that is spelled out is a service
phrases.notes: The detail is 'זבח', slaughtering.

phrases.english: and we require it to be for their sake,
phrases.notes: Here 'for their sake' means for the sake of the owner, which is the topic of this discussion.

phrases.english: so too every service, we require it to be for their sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל וּפְרָט וּכְלָל – אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the objection answered, רבינא completes the derivation he began in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Step 8: Where do we learn that קבלה must be for the owner?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the כלל ופרט וכלל in the נזיר's ram פסוק: every עבודה like שחיטה must be for the owner.

steps.title: Maybe only services punished outside the Temple are included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the derivation. Perhaps the shared feature is that one is liable for doing the service outside. That would include שחיטה and זריקה but leave out קבלה and הולכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe: just as the detail spelled out is a service for which one is liable when doing it outside, so too only services for which one is liable outside are included. Then slaughtering and sprinkling are included, but collecting and carrying the blood are not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions which feature of the detail we should copy. A different feature would leave קבלה out, which defeats the whole proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה has more than one feature. It is a service, and it also carries a penalty when done outside the Temple. If we copy the stricter feature, only שחיטה and זריקה qualify, and קבלה is excluded again. This is the same stricter feature that blocked us in Step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for doing it outside the Temple
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Collecting the blood in a vessel
Carrying the blood to the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This step attacks only the choice of feature taken from the detail. It does not attack the כלל ופרט וכלל structure, which was already defended in Step 15.

phrases.english: Or perhaps: just as the detail spelled out is a service
and one is liable for it when done outside,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל עֲבוֹדָה וְחַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ בַּחוּץ;
phrases.english: so too only a service for which one is liable when done outside;
slaughtering and sprinkling — yes,
collecting and carrying — no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה הַפְּרָט מְפוֹרָשׁ – עֲבוֹדָה וְחַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the feature רבינא chose from the detail in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of 'עבודה' as the shared feature in רבינא's כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The detail also has the stricter feature of liability for doing it outside. Using that feature includes only שחיטה and זריקה and excludes קבלה.

steps.title: Another possible shared feature: services done in the north
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second way to define what the detail has in common with what it includes. Under this reading, שחיטה and קבלה are included, but זריקה is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe we should say: the detail, slaughter, is a service that must be done in the north of the courtyard and is also part of the inner חטאות. So we include every service that is done in the north and is part of the inner חטאות. That includes slaughter and collection, but not sprinkling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still challenging רבינא's derivation. It gives another way to say what the detail has in common with the other services, and this way leaves out זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a כלל ופרט וכלל we include only things that are like the detail, but there is more than one way to say what "like" means. In step 17 the shared feature was being liable for doing the service outside, which includes זריקה and leaves out קבלה. Here the shared feature is being done in the north and being part of the inner חטאות, which includes קבלה and leaves out זריקה. So the two readings clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or else
The northern part of the עזרה, where some קרבנות must be slaughtered
Inner sin offerings, whose blood is brought inside the היכל
Collecting the animal's blood in a sacred vessel
Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: Alternatively,
just as the detail is clearly defined as
an action that requires the north
and is found in the inner sin offerings,
so too, anything that requires the north
and is found in the inner sin offerings is included;
slaughter and collection: yes,
sprinkling: no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, מָה הַפְּרָט מְפוֹרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, competing way to define the shared feature, on top of the one in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the כלל ופרט וכלל includes every service, including קבלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The shared feature could just as well be services done in the north that are part of the inner חטאות. That would include קבלה but exclude זריקה, so it is unclear what the derivation really includes.

steps.title: Both readings are equal, so both services are included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both ways of defining the shared feature are equally strong, so both קבלה and זריקה are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say it this way, and you can say it that way. Since they are equal, both are included. Another version: each one stays in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the two challenges together. Since neither reading is stronger, we do not choose between them. We include everything each reading includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17's reading includes זריקה, and step 18's reading includes קבלה. Since the two readings are equally strong, the גמרא includes both services. The other version says the same thing in different words: each service keeps its place in the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They are equally balanced
And both are included
Another version of the wording
Here: stays in place, keeps its status

steps.confusionAlert: The word תיקו here does NOT mean the usual "the question is left unresolved." Here it means that each service keeps its place, so both stay included.

phrases.english: One can say it this way
and one can say it that way;
they are equal,
so both are included.
Another version:
and each one stays in its status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר הָכִי וְאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two competing readings from steps 17 and 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both readings are equally strong, so the derivation includes what each one includes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We would have to pick one shared feature, and then either קבלה or זריקה would be left out
steps.terutzMaskana: Both readings count equally, so both קבלה and זריקה must be done for the owner

steps.title: Sprinkling is already learned from רב אשי's verse
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: זריקה already has its own source in רב אשי's פסוק, so the כלל ופרט וכלל must be coming to include קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead: sprinkling is learned from the source of רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the clash between the two readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זריקה is already known to need the owner's sake from the פסוק רב אשי quoted earlier in step 4. So there is no need for the כלל ופרט וכלל to teach זריקה. It must be teaching קבלה, which fits the reading in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say; introduces another answer
Is derived; comes out from

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
sprinkling is learned from the source of רב אשי.
phrases.notes: That is the פסוק רב אשי quoted back in step 4, "ונרצה לו לכפר עליו" (ויקרא 1:4).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: זְרִיקָה – מִדְּרַב אָשֵׁי נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same problem that step 19 answered
steps.terutzResolutionType: זריקה has a separate source, so the derivation is used for קבלה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כלל ופרט וכלל might be teaching זריקה and not קבלה
steps.terutzMaskana: זריקה comes from רב אשי's פסוק, and the כלל ופרט וכלל includes קבלה
steps.whatToRemember: Every service, including קבלה and זריקה, must be done for the owner. You can see this in two ways: both readings of the derivation count equally, or זריקה comes from רב אשי's פסוק and the derivation adds קבלה.

steps.title: From the נזיר's ram to all other peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The rule so far was learned only for the נזיר's ram. The גמרא asks for a source that applies it to all other שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the ram of a נזיר. From where do we learn it for other peace offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. The source so far speaks only about the נזיר's ram, so it asks how we know the rule for every other שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole derivation came from a פסוק about the ram a נזיר brings. A פסוק about one specific קרבן does not automatically teach about other קרבנות of the same kind. So the גמרא now looks for a way to extend the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
The ram that a נזיר brings as a שלמים at the end of his נזירות
All other peace offerings
From where do we know?

phrases.english: We found a source for the ram of a נזיר;
from where do we learn it for other peace offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן אֵיל נְזִיר, שְׁאָר שְׁלָמִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the finished derivation for the נזיר's ram and asks how to extend it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that all שלמים, not just the נזיר's ram, must be offered for the sake of the owner

steps.title: Why we cannot simply learn all peace offerings from the איל נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning all שלמים from the איל נזיר, then rejects that idea. The איל נזיר is special because other קרבנות are brought together with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let us learn it from the ram of a נזיר. That does not work. The ram of a נזיר is special, because other offerings are brought along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a simple answer to the question from step 21: just learn all שלמים from the איל נזיר. Then it knocks that answer down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To learn one case from another, the source case must not have a special feature that could explain its law. The איל נזיר comes as part of a package with a חטאת and an עולה. So maybe only it needs the special intent, and ordinary שלמים do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn it (from another case)
The ram a נזיר brings as a שלמים at the end of his נזירות
'What about...?' The opening of a challenge that points out what makes the source case special
Literally 'other blood': other קרבנות brought together with it

phrases.english: And if you will say: let us learn it from the ram of a nazir
What about the ram of a nazir?
It is special, since there is other blood with them!
phrases.notes: 'Other blood' means other offerings: the נזיר also brings a חטאת and an עולה along with his ram.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא נֵילַף מֵאֵיל נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and then refutes an obvious answer to the question asked in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea of learning all שלמים from the איל נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איל נזיר has a unique feature: other קרבנות come with it. That feature could explain its strict rule, so the rule cannot be carried over to ordinary שלמים.

steps.title: The word שלמים includes all peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says שלמים and not שלמיו ('his שלמים'). The extra wide wording teaches that the rule covers all שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the rule were only for the נזיר's ram, the Torah should have written 'his שלמים.' Why does it say just 'שלמים'? To include all שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 21 from the wording of the פסוק itself. It no longer needs to compare one case to another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק is about the נזיר, the natural word would be שלמיו, 'his שלמים.' The Torah instead used the general word שלמים. That broad wording shows the rule is not limited to the נזיר, so the problem raised in step 22 no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your claim were true
His שלמים (a form that ties the word to one person)
To include (more cases)

steps.whatToRemember: All שלמים, not just the איל נזיר, must be offered for their own sake and for the sake of their owners. This is learned from the general word שלמים.

phrases.english: If so, let it write 'his peace offerings'
What is 'peace offerings' for? To include all peace offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב שְׁלָמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the refutation of step 22 by finding the source in the פסוק's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the extra or general wording of the פסוק as an inclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule may apply only to the איל נזיר, which is special because other קרבנות come with it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general word שלמים, used instead of שלמיו, includes all שלמים.

steps.title: What is the source for all other offerings?
steps.stepSummary: We now have a source for all שלמים. The גמרא asks where we learn the rule for every other kind of קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for שלמים. Where do we learn it for all the other קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves the search one level wider, from שלמים to every type of קרבן. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, every source has been about שלמים. The rule is meant to apply to all קרבנות, so the גמרא needs a source that reaches beyond שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for)
All other קרבנות
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found it for peace offerings;
from where do we know it for all other offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן שְׁלָמִים, שְׁאָר כׇּל קֳדָשִׁים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of step 23 and widens the question to all קרבנות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that all קדשים, not only שלמים, must be offered for their own sake and for the sake of their owners.

steps.title: Why we cannot learn all offerings from peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning all קדשים from שלמים, then rejects it. שלמים have three special requirements: סמיכה, נסכים, and תנופת חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let us learn it from שלמים. That does not work. שלמים are special, because they need סמיכה, נסכים, and the waving of the breast and the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simple answer to step 24's question: learn all other קרבנות from שלמים. Then it rejects that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same method as step 22, one level higher. שלמים have extra requirements that not all other קרבנות share. So the strict rule about intent might belong only to such a special קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner pressing his hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
Wine and flour offerings that accompany the קרבן
Waving the breast and the thigh of the animal

steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that every other קרבן lacks all three. Some other קרבנות have one of these features. The point is that שלמים have all three together, so they are special.

phrases.english: And if you will say: let us learn it from peace offerings,
what about peace offerings? They are special, since they require placing of hands
and libations and waving of the breast and thigh!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא נֵילַף מִשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and then refutes an obvious answer to the question of step 24, using the same pattern as step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea of learning all קדשים from שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמים have a unique combination of requirements: סמיכה, נסכים, and תנופת חזה ושוק. These could explain their strict rule, so it cannot be carried over to all other קרבנות.

steps.title: All offerings are linked to שלמים by the פסוק of 'זאת התורה'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'זאת התורה' lists every type of קרבן alongside שלמים. That linking (a היקש) teaches that all קרבנות need לשמה for both the type of offering and the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק says: 'This is the law of the עולה, the מנחה, the חטאת, the אשם, the מילואים, and the זבח השלמים.' The Torah linked them all to שלמים. Just as שלמים must be done for their own sake, both regarding the type of offering and regarding the owner, so too every קרבן must be done for its own sake in both ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to the question of Step 24: where do we learn the לשמה rule for all other קרבנות? It uses a פסוק that lists all the קרבנות together with שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 25, learning from שלמים by logic failed because שלמים have special features. Now the source is a היקש, a link written directly into the פסוק itself. A היקש cannot be pushed away by pointing to differences, so every קרבן takes on the rule of שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A link the Torah makes by listing things together, so they share the same rules
Changing the type of offering in one's mind, for example thinking 'this is a שלמים' about an עולה
Changing the owner in one's mind, meaning offering it for someone other than its real owner
For its own sake: with the correct intention for this offering and this owner
The special inauguration offerings brought when the משכן was first set up

steps.whatToRemember: The source for לשמה in all קרבנות is the היקש in 'זאת התורה', which links every offering to שלמים.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 25 rejected learning from שלמים by logic. Here the גמרא still learns from שלמים, but through a היקש written in the פסוק. A היקש works even when the cases are different.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long search that began in Step 21. The לשמה requirement now covers every קרבן, for both the type of offering and the owner.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"This is the law of the burnt offering and of the meal offering,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:37

phrases.english: and of the sin offering and of the guilt offering,
and of the inauguration offerings and of the sacrifice of peace offerings" –
the verse linked them to peace offerings;

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים – בֵּין שִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ בֵּין שִׁינּוּי בְעָלִים,
phrases.english: just as with peace offerings, whether a change of offering type or a change of owner,
we require it to be for its own sake;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל בֵּין שִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ בֵּין שִׁינּוּי בְעָלִים,
phrases.english: so too with all offerings, whether a change of offering type or a change of owner,
we require it to be for its own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in Step 25 with a היקש from the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have tried to learn all קרבנות from שלמים by logic, but שלמים have special features, so that failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק itself links all קרבנות to שלמים, so all of them need לשמה for both type and owner.

steps.title: If לשמה is required, why isn't a wrong-intention offering invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: since לשמה is a requirement, a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה should be completely פסול. Yet the משנה says it is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that when someone slaughters them not for their own sake, they should be disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has proven that לשמה is required, it challenges the משנה. The משנה rules that such a קרבן is still כשר, only it does not count for the owner's obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if the Torah requires something and you don't do it, the act is invalid. So if לשמה is a real requirement, the logical result is פסול. The גמרא wants to know what source makes the קרבן stay valid anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake: with the wrong intention
Let them be disqualified
Say: introduces a suggested conclusion that seems to follow

phrases.english: Say that where one slaughtered them
not for their own sake – they should be disqualified!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא הֵיכָא דְּשָׁחֵיט לְהוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ לִיפַּסְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the requirement proven in Step 26 and asks why breaking it doesn't make the קרבן invalid.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the משנה that offerings slaughtered שלא לשמה are כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If לשמה is a Torah requirement, failing to do it should make the offering פסול.

steps.title: 'מוצא שפתיך': a failed vow-offering becomes a נדבה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls a vow-offering a נדבה. This teaches that if it was offered properly it counts as the נדר, and if not, it is still a valid נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'What comes out of your lips you shall keep and do, as you vowed...' Is this a נדבה? It is a נדר! Rather, it means: if you did as you vowed, it counts as your נדר. If not, it is a נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק. That פסוק shows that a קרבן offered wrongly does not become פסול; it just changes into a voluntary gift-offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a נדר but uses the word נדבה, which seems contradictory. The גמרא explains that the Torah is describing two outcomes. Done properly, it pays off the vow. Done wrongly, for example שלא לשמה, it is still a valid offering, but the owner has not fulfilled his vow.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes out of your lips: the words of a vow
A vow-offering, which the owner is responsible for until it is brought properly
A gift-offering, a voluntary קרבן with no obligation attached

steps.whatToRemember: A קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמה is still כשר as a נדבה, but it does not fulfill the owner's obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's ruling that such קרבנות are valid but do not count for the owner.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"What comes out of your lips you shall keep
phrases.notes: דברים 23:24

phrases.english: and do, as you vowed, etc." –
phrases.notes: The word נדבה is in the part of the פסוק hidden behind 'etc.': '...as you vowed to ה׳ your God, a נדבה.'

phrases.english: Is this a gift-offering?! It is a vow-offering!

phrases.aramaic: [אֶלָּא] אִם כְּמָה שֶׁנָּדַרְתָּ עָשִׂיתָ – יְהֵא נֶדֶר,
phrases.english: Rather, if you did as you vowed – it shall be a vow-offering,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and if not – it shall be a gift-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ תִּשְׁמֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27 by showing that the Torah keeps the improper offering valid.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source showing a changed outcome rather than invalidity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Breaking the לשמה requirement should make the קרבן פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah itself says an improperly brought vow-offering becomes a valid נדבה, so it is כשר but does not fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: Why both פסוקים are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why the Torah needed both 'מוצא שפתיך' and 'זאת התורה'. It starts with what we would have thought if only 'מוצא' were written.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both 'מוצא שפתיך' and 'זאת התורה' were needed. For if the Torah had written only 'מוצא', I would have said...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to explain why each of the two פסוקים is necessary, and the explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think one פסוק could teach everything, so the גמרא shows that each one adds something. Here it begins with the first half: what we would have mistakenly concluded with only 'מוצא שפתיך'. The actual mistaken idea comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed: introduces an explanation of why each source is necessary
The Merciful One: a name for ה׳, as the giver of the Torah
I would have said: introduces a mistaken first assumption

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "what comes out of your lips,"
and it was necessary to write "this is the law";
for if the Merciful One had written only "what comes out" –
I would have said
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having used two פסוקים (Steps 26 and 28), the גמרא begins to justify why both are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both 'מוצא שפתיך' and 'זאת התורה' are necessary; the explanation begins with what we would assume from 'מוצא' alone.
